name: Antigua and Barbuda
prevalence_note: Government of Antigua and Barbuda, Royal Police Force (RPFAB) & ECCB 2025-2026: social-engineering bank phishing/OTP calls, WhatsApp relative and customs parcel impersonation, and ECCU lottery/crypto pyramid scams dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-268 within NANP and the ECCU; overseas scammers spoof +1 numbers and hijack local WhatsApp profiles to target residents.

scams.name: Bank Account Social-Engineering Vishing & Phishing Link Scam
scams.name_en: Fake bank representative creating artificial urgency to capture logins, card details, or OTPs
scams.signals_en: Social engineer impersonates an Antigua bank warning of dire account consequences unless the victim immediately clicks a link or shares login/OTP details.
scams.legit_en: Antigua government cybersecurity guidance and ECCB stress always verifying urgent requests by calling a known bank number independently.
bait_tactics: Tell them you will pause a moment and call the St. John's branch helpline printed on the back of your card.
Pretend your internet is down and ask them to spell out their department name slowly.
Ask which branch you visited last month without giving them any personal details.

scams.name: RPFAB-Warned WhatsApp Impersonation & Customs Parcel Fee Scam
scams.name_en: Cloned WhatsApp friend/relative asking for urgent wire or customs barrel clearance money
scams.signals_en: Message or call from a hijacked WhatsApp account or new number claiming to be a relative needing urgent travel cash or a customs clearance fee wired to a third party.
scams.legit_en: RPFAB urges residents to verify any WhatsApp money or customs request via a direct voice call to the contact's known number.
bait_tactics: Ask a personal family question about Antigua that an impersonator would never know.
Say you will go to Deep Water Harbour or V.C. Bird Airport customs counter yourself.
Refuse to send any verification code and ring the person's old saved line.

scams.name: ECCB-Warned Lottery Advance-Fee & Unlicensed Crypto Scam
scams.name_en: Fake lottery prize demanding upfront payment or unlicensed zero-risk crypto investment club
scams.signals_en: Caller claims the victim won an overseas lottery requiring a tax/fee wire, or pitches an unlicensed high-return crypto recruitment programme.
scams.legit_en: ECCB advises checking ECSRC licensing before any investment and never paying upfront fees to claim prizes.
bait_tactics: Ask for their ECSRC licence status and official St. John's registered office.
Suggest they deduct the processing charge straight from the prize money.
Pretend you need time to find a calculator and ask them to explain the fee breakdown again.
